title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of category M2 or M3 vehicles with regard to their general construction
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types of category M2 or M3 (buses and coaches) with regard to their general construction. It also approves bodywork types as separate technical units, vehicles fitted with already-approved bodywork, and fire suppression systems as components. It applies to single-deck, double-deck, rigid and articulated vehicles, with exclusions for certain special-purpose vehicles.
scope_quote: 1.1 This Regulation applies to every single-deck, double-deck, rigid or articulated vehicle of category M2 or M3. 1.2 However, the requirements of this Regulation do not apply to the following vehicles: 1.2.1 Vehicles designed for the secure transport of persons, for example prisoners; 1.2.2 Vehicles specially designed for the carriage of injured or sick persons (ambulances); 1.2.3 Off-road vehicles. 1.2.4 Vehicles specially designed for the carriage of school children.
applies_to_components: fire suppression system (component; engine compartment fire detection and suppression)
service doors (power-operated, automatically-operated, driver-operated, sliding, double doors)
emergency doors, emergency windows, escape hatches
passenger seats, priority seats, demountable seats
wheelchair spaces and wheelchair stability/restraint provisions
guarding of step wells and exposed seats
steps, gangways, access passages, intercommunication staircases, half staircases
safety signs and visual contrast of markings
trolleybus current collector, traction and auxiliary electrical equipment, wiring and apparatus
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories M2 and M3 as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6.
Approval mark may be combined with the marks of other UN Regulations under which the vehicle is approved (paragraph 4.5).
Paragraph 1.4: Contracting Parties may set national requirements for audible and/or visual route and destination display equipment pending UN provisions.
Superstructure is defined with reference to roll-over strength (the subject of UN R66).

defined_terms.definition: A vehicle of category M2 or M3 within the scope of paragraph 1.
Vehicle with more than 22 passengers constructed with areas for standing passengers, to allow frequent passenger movement.
Vehicle with more than 22 passengers constructed principally for seated passengers, allowing standing passengers in the gangway and/or an area not exceeding two double seats.
Vehicle with more than 22 passengers constructed exclusively for the carriage of seated passengers.
Vehicle with not more than 22 passengers designed to carry standing passengers, having seats and provision for standing passengers.
Vehicle with not more than 22 passengers not designed to carry standing passengers.
A vehicle of two or more permanently connected, intercommunicating rigid sections that articulate relative to one another.
An articulated vehicle whose sections intercommunicate on at least one deck.
A Class I, II or A vehicle in which at least 35 per cent of the standing area forms a step-free area including access to at least one service door.
A separate technical unit comprising all the special internal and external equipment of the vehicle.
A vehicle whose passenger spaces are at least partly on two superimposed levels, with no standing space on the upper deck.
A device intended to be part of a vehicle which may be type-approved separately, but only in relation to specified vehicle types.
A vehicle electrically driven by energy from external overhead contact wires, including dual mode and guided trolleybuses.
A vehicle without roof over all or part of its (upper) deck, on which no standing space may be provided.
Fire suppression systems, approved as components, not differing in manufacturer, extinguishing agent, type of discharge point or type of propellant gas.
The part of the bodywork which contributes to the strength of the vehicle in a roll-over accident.
A door intended for use by passengers in normal circumstances with the driver seated.
A door affording two, or the equivalent of two, access passages.
A door opened or closed only by sliding it along one or more (approximately) rectilinear rails.
A door intended for use by passengers as an exit only exceptionally, in particular in an emergency.
A window, not necessarily glazed, intended for use as an exit by passengers in an emergency only.
An emergency window divisible into two or more parts each complying with the requirements for a normal emergency window.
An opening in the roof or floor intended for use as an emergency exit only.
An emergency door, emergency window or escape hatch.
A service door, intercommunication staircase, half-staircase or emergency exit.
The part of the bodywork whose upper surface supports standing passengers, seated passengers' feet, the driver and crew, and possibly seat mountings.
The part of the floor provided only for passengers.
The space giving passengers access between seats, wheelchair areas, access passages, staircases and standing areas, with specified exclusions.
The space extending inwards from the service door to the outermost edge of the upper step, intercommunication staircase or half-staircase.
The space for the driver's exclusive use containing the driver's seat, steering wheel, controls and instruments.
Any passenger with difficulty using public transport, e.g. disabled or elderly people, pregnant women, people with children, pushchairs or heavy luggage.
A person who due to infirmity or disability uses a wheelchair for mobility.
Space for passengers' use excluding fixed appliances such as bars, kitchenettes, toilets or baggage compartments.
A service door operated exclusively by non-muscular energy, remotely controlled by the driver or crew if not automatic.
A power-operated service door opened only after a passenger control and driver activation, which closes again automatically.
A device which prevents the vehicle being driven away from rest when a door is not fully closed.
A service door normally opened and closed by the driver.
A seat with additional space for a passenger with reduced mobility and marked accordingly.
A device to facilitate wheelchair access to vehicles, such as lifts or ramps.
A system which lowers and lifts totally or partially the vehicle body relative to the normal travel position.
A device or system with a platform raised and lowered to give access between the passenger compartment floor and the ground or kerb.
A device bridging the gap between the passenger compartment floor and the ground or kerb, including any surface over which a wheelchair travels when deployed.
A ramp detachable from the vehicle structure and deployable by the driver or crew member.
A seat that can be easily detached from the vehicle.
A staircase allowing communication between the upper and lower decks.
A space occupied by passengers or crew in use which is separated from other passenger or crew spaces.
A staircase from the upper deck which terminates in an emergency door.
Lighting device(s) designed to illuminate the exterior vicinity of service doors and wheels.
A system to secure the service and emergency doors of the vehicle against opening.
A system providing minimum lighting to enable occupants to safely egress the vehicle, including the emergency exits.
A configuration of visual elements intended to convey a safety-related message.
The brightness (luminance) ratio between an object and its immediate background allowing it to be distinguished.

applicability_hints: Engine compartment fire detection/suppression systems can be type-approved separately as components under R107 (Annex 13) and must bear an R107 approval mark on their main part.
A bus bodywork can be approved as a separate technical unit (mark with letter S) only for specified vehicle (chassis) types; the assembler of chassis plus approved bodywork is the manufacturer.
Wheelchair lifts, ramps (incl. portable ramps) and kneeling systems are covered via Annex 8 and the reactive-force tests of Annex 6.
Power-operated and automatic service doors, their controls, starting prevention devices, closing-force/anti-trap behaviour and overnight locking systems are covered by Annex 3 7.6 and Annex 6.
Interior lighting, emergency lighting systems, service-door lighting and safety signs/markings (visual contrast, Annex 5) fall under R107 installation requirements.
Passenger seats, priority seats, demountable seats, handrails, handholds, step-well guards, trap doors and passenger entertainment screens are addressed by Annex 3 / Annex 8.
Wheelchair restraint arrangements and pram/pushchair spaces are addressed in Annex 8.
Trolleybus current collectors, traction and auxiliary electrical equipment and wiring are subject to Annex 12.

Excluded: prisoner transport vehicles, ambulances, off-road vehicles and vehicles specially designed for school children; police/armed-forces vehicles and stationary-use vehicles (e.g. mobile libraries) only as compatible with use.
Route/destination display equipment is not regulated by R107 (national requirements allowed).
Superstructure (roll-over strength) is defined here but tested under a separate regulation.
